modifications: Copied the best-first DFlash lattice search into an mlx2 experiment module.
Added a default-off adapter that loads the pinned TensorFold kernels from a declared local source checkout and applies them to mlx2-owned model weights and caches.
Kept the existing mlx2 ordinary and external-chain routes as the reference paths.

Bridge task 1 (MLX2_TENSORFOLD_CACHE_EXECUTOR): validate the pinned revision once per resolved source root, eagerly import every kernel module the tree forward and commit use, refuse a module imported from another root, and install the capture-layer storage once per model and tap set. Original mlx2 code; no TensorFold source copied.

Bridge task 2 (block-8 lattice) was measured and rejected, and its gate removed: TensorFold's tree mode keeps DFlashProposer.tree_block = 16 and uses the block-size lattice only in chain mode (DraftSlot.get with chains=True), so the pre-existing mlx2 depth-16 lattice already matched the pinned source. The draft API keeps a lattice_positions parameter defaulting to 16.

Bridge task 2b (MLX2_DFLASH_TREE_CODEBOOK_CACHE): cache float32 host copies of the selector codebooks once per draft instance, the design of DFlashProposer._codebooks at the pinned revision; rebuilt when either weight array is replaced.

Omitted from the mlx2 tree builder, on purpose, to keep the proposal policy fixed across bridge arms: TensorFold's sampled-mode Gumbel lattice noise (tree_noise 0.7, unary / temperature, keyed uniform_rows), its session n-gram prior (disabled in its Qwen3.5 DraftSlot anyway), its copy/branch proposer, and by_chance calibrated reordering. mlx2 keeps edge 0.6, tau 1.5, children 4, max_nodes 15 with no noise at any temperature.
Bridge tasks 3-5 (batched target laws, on-request logprobs, single fence) are original mlx2 code over mlx2's own verifier and sampling transform; TensorFold's keyed-noise sampling is not used.

Rejected and removed after measurement: an mx.compile of each DFlash2 layer's fixed-shape conv/norm/MLP parts, the design of DFlashProposer._compiled_parts at the pinned revision. It left lattice wait unchanged.

Bridge task 7 (MLX2_TREE_PIPELINE_DRAFT) is original mlx2 code. It follows TensorFold's idea of queueing the next lattice before the round finishes (DFlashProposer._start_tree/_finish_tree split); mlx2 queues it after the committed round, on a descriptor copy of the draft cache, and adopts it only inside the next round's transaction when the committed boundary matches.
Batched presence-penalty contract: original mlx2 code. make_presence_penalty declares presence_window, and the batched verifier applies it per tree row.

Bounded multi-lane target executor: original mlx2 control-plane code. The singleton default preserves historical execution; a revision-bound tensorfold_cohort_limit policy explicitly selects 1..4 lanes only with the TensorFold target. Parents, caches, accepted paths, RNG streams and recovery snapshots remain lane-owned. The ordinary/reference target route is unchanged.

2026-10-05 packed target correction: forward_many now calls the pinned TensorFold lane_multi.multi_tree_forward and commit_streams primitives directly instead of invoking lane_tree.tree_forward once per lane behind one fence. TensorFold concatenates real tree rows, executes row-local projections and MLP over the packed axis, applies per-stream attention and recurrent plans against independent caches, then groups recurrent commit replay. No TensorFold source was copied; mlx2 adapts shapes, capture taps, transactions, receipts and failure closure around the pinned MIT implementation.
validation: Focused CPU topology and acceptance tests.
TensorFold public four-cell fixture with per-arm mechanism counters and thermal receipts.
qualification/runs/tensorfold-upstream-parity-20260928/bridge/check_tree_exactness.py (GPU gates 1-4) and per-arm public-fixture receipts under bridge/.

tests/test_dflash_tree_bridge.py (CPU): executor cache, bounded multi-lane cache/parent/path ownership, multi-lane token and RNG parity against the ordinary tree reference, partial-commit recovery of every lane, lattice positions, codebook cache, batched-vs-row laws (including presence penalty) at every accepted depth 0..15 and on non-prefix branches, logprobs, single fence, pipelined draft, phase timing, and fault injection at five round phases in row, batched and pipelined modes.
qualification/runs/tensorfold-upstream-parity-20260928/bridge/RESULTS.md: interleaved all-off vs all-on A/B, 3x3 arms, 62.40 -> 95.22 tok/s (+52.6%), thermal 0, no swapouts.

qualification/runs/tensorfold-coalescing-20260930/tree-cohort-ab-long-20260930-1140/campaign.json: valid Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4e-mtp Metal A/B at concurrency 4 and 256 generated tokens per request. Cohort width 4 engaged for 200 rounds and 685 lanes with output hashes equal to the singleton arm, but batch goodput was 0.9417x on code and 0.9962x on chat. Thermal state remained 0 and swapouts did not change. The cohort limit therefore remains explicitly selectable but defaults to 1 and is not qualified or selected.

qualification/runs/dflash-packed-target-correction-20261005: current-source B2 and B4 adapter-default spot checks observed one physical packed target forward per cohort round, output hashes matching B1 for both prompts, and clean paired-lock restoration. A skewed B4 run also observed independent per-stream commits with packed target execution. These were one-repetition diagnostics, not controlled performance qualification.
